grammar.title: Present Continuous (and Present Simple vs Continuous)
grammar.explanation:
We use the **present continuous** for actions happening **now**.
Look at this sentence: I **am reading** about films now.

Make it with **am / is / are + verb-ing**.
I **am reading**. She **is reading**. They **are reading**.

We also use it for things happening around now.
I **am reading** a book about an action film this week.

We use the **present simple** for habits.
I go to the bank every Monday. But now I **am going** to the bank.

Some verbs are not actions, and we do not use them in the continuous.
We say I **know** the answer. Never say "I am knowing".
examples: *We **aren't watching** the film. You can turn it off.* (film — like our action film!)

practice.q: My brother cleans the bathroom every day. (Say it is happening NOW.)
practice.a: My brother is cleaning the bathroom now.

practice.q: I read with my bedside lamp every night. (Say it is happening NOW.)
practice.a: I am reading with my bedside lamp now.

practice.q: They watch an action film. (Say they are NOT watching now.)
practice.a: They aren't watching an action film now.

practice.q: She works at the bank today. (Make a question.)
practice.a: Is she working at the bank today?
